wikitext.*: {{short description|American college basketball season}} {{Use American English|date=March 2026}} {{Use mdy dates|date=August 2023}} {{Infobox NCAA team season |mode=Basketball |year=2020–21 |team=Coppin State Eagles |image= |image_size=150 |conference=Mid-Eastern Athletic Conference |division=Northern Division |short_conf=MEAC |CoachRank= |APRank= |record=9–13 |conf_record=8–4 |head_coach=[[Juan Dixon]] |hc_year=4th |assoc_coach=John Auslander |asst_coach1=Charles Agumagu |asst_coach2=[[Kevin Braswell]] |stadium=[[Physical Education Complex]] |champion=MEAC North division co-champions |bowl= |bowl_result= }} {{2020–21 MEAC men's basketball standings}} The '''2020–21 Coppin State Eagles men's basketball team''' represented [[Coppin State University]] in the [[2020–21 NCAA Division I men's basketball season]]. The Eagles, led by fourth-year head coach [[Juan Dixon]], played their home games at the [[Physical Education Complex]] in [[Baltimore|Baltimore, Maryland]] as members of the [[Mid-Eastern Athletic Conference]]. With the creation of divisions to cut down on travel due to the [[COVID-19 pandemic in the United States|COVID-19 pandemic]], they played in the Northern Division.{{Cite news|url=https://meacsports.com/news/2020/12/14/meac-announces-revised-conference-schedules-for-mens-womens-basketball.aspx|title=MEAC Announces Revised Conference Schedules for Men's, Women's Basketball|work=Mid-Eastern Athletic Conference|date=December 14, 2020|accessdate=January 4, 2021|language=en}} ==Previous season== The [[2019–20 Coppin State Eagles men's basketball team|Eagles]] finished the [[2019–20 NCAA Division I men's basketball season|2019–20 season]] 11–20, 7–9 in MEAC play to finish in seventh place. They were scheduled to play against [[2019–20 Norfolk State Spartans men's basketball team|Norfolk State]] in the quarterfinals of the [[2020 MEAC men's basketball tournament|MEAC tournament]], but the remainder of the tournament was cancelled due to the ongoing [[COVID-19 pandemic in the United States|COVID-19 pandemic]].{{Cite
